Exercise 15.7.50 — Mass, Center of Mass, and Moment of Inertia

Problem. If EEE is the solid bounded by the cylinder y2+z2=9y^2 + z^2 = 9y2+z2=9 and the planes x=0x = 0x=0, y=3xy = 3xy=3x, and z=0z = 0z=0 in the first octant, with density function ρ(x,y,z)=x2+y2\rho(x,y,z) = x^2 + y^2ρ(x,y,z)=x2+y2, find, correct to three decimal places, (a) the mass, (b) the center of mass, (c) the moment of inertia about the zzz-axis.

The center of mass is (xˉ,yˉ,zˉ)=(Myz/M, Mxz/M, Mxy/M)(\bar x, \bar y, \bar z) = (M_{yz}/M,\, M_{xz}/M,\, M_{xy}/M)(xˉ,yˉ​,zˉ)=(Myz​/M,Mxz​/M,Mxy​/M).

Part 1 — The mass

Step 1.1: Describe the solid.

The solid lies in the first octant inside the cylinder y2+z2=9y^2 + z^2 = 9y2+z2=9, behind the plane x=0x = 0x=0, in front of the plane x=y/3x = y/3x=y/3 (i.e. y=3xy = 3xy=3x), and above z=0z = 0z=0. In polar coordinates in the yzyzyz-plane, y=rcos⁡θy = r\cos\thetay=rcosθ, z=rsin⁡θz = r\sin\thetaz=rsinθ, the base is the quarter disk 0≤θ≤π/20 \le \theta \le \pi/20≤θ≤π/2, 0≤r≤30 \le r \le 30≤r≤3, and the extent in xxx is 0≤x≤y/3=rcos⁡θ/30 \le x \le y/3 = r\cos\theta/30≤x≤y/3=rcosθ/3:

E={(x,r,θ):0≤θ≤π/2,  0≤r≤3,  0≤x≤rcos⁡θ3}. E = \{(x,r,\theta): 0 \le \theta \le \pi/2,\; 0 \le r \le 3,\; 0 \le x \le \tfrac{r\cos\theta}{3}\}. E={(x,r,θ):0≤θ≤π/2,0≤r≤3,0≤x≤3rcosθ​}.

Step 1.2: Set up the mass integral.

With ρ=x2+y2=x2+r2cos⁡2θ\rho = x^2 + y^2 = x^2 + r^2\cos^2\thetaρ=x2+y2=x2+r2cos2θ and Jacobian rrr:

M=∫0π/2 ⁣∫03 ⁣∫0rcos⁡θ/3(x2+r2cos⁡2θ) r dx dr dθ. M = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\int_0^3\!\int_0^{r\cos\theta/3} (x^2 + r^2\cos^2\theta)\, r\, dx\, dr\, d\theta. M=∫0π/2​∫03​∫0rcosθ/3​(x2+r2cos2θ)rdxdrdθ.

Step 1.3: Evaluate with SymPy.

The script solution/part1_step1.py evaluates this iterated integral exactly with SymPy:

M=565=11.2. M = \frac{56}{5} = 11.2. M=556​=11.2.

Result (a). The mass is M=565=11.200. M = \frac{56}{5} = 11.200. M=556​=11.200.

Part 2 — The center of mass

Step 2.1: Evaluate the first moments.

With the same limits, the three first moments are Myz=∭Exρ dVM_{yz} = \iiint_E x\rho\, dVMyz​=∭E​xρdV, Mxz=∭Eyρ dVM_{xz} = \iiint_E y\rho\, dVMxz​=∭E​yρdV, Mxy=∭Ezρ dVM_{xy} = \iiint_E z\rho\, dVMxy​=∭E​zρdV, where the weights are xxx, y=rcos⁡θy = r\cos\thetay=rcosθ, z=rsin⁡θz = r\sin\thetaz=rsinθ. The script solution/part2_step2.py evaluates all four integrals exactly with SymPy:

M=565,Myz=171π128,Mxz=63π8,Mxy=212. M = \frac{56}{5}, \qquad M_{yz} = \frac{171\pi}{128}, \qquad M_{xz} = \frac{63\pi}{8}, \qquad M_{xy} = \frac{21}{2}. M=556​,Myz​=128171π​,Mxz​=863π​,Mxy​=221​.

Step 2.2: Divide by the mass.

xˉ=MyzM=855π7168≈0.3747296,yˉ=MxzM=45π64≈2.2089323,zˉ=MxyM=1516=0.9375. \bar x = \frac{M_{yz}}{M} = \frac{855\pi}{7168} \approx 0.3747296, \qquad \bar y = \frac{M_{xz}}{M} = \frac{45\pi}{64} \approx 2.2089323, \qquad \bar z = \frac{M_{xy}}{M} = \frac{15}{16} = 0.9375. xˉ=MMyz​​=7168855π​≈0.3747296,yˉ​=MMxz​​=6445π​≈2.2089323,zˉ=MMxy​​=1615​=0.9375.

The script checks that the point lies inside the solid: 0≤xˉ≤yˉ/30 \le \bar x \le \bar y/30≤xˉ≤yˉ​/3, yˉ,zˉ≥0\bar y, \bar z \ge 0yˉ​,zˉ≥0, and yˉ2+zˉ2≤9\bar y^2 + \bar z^2 \le 9yˉ​2+zˉ2≤9.

Result (b). To three decimal places, the center of mass is (xˉ,yˉ,zˉ)≈(0.375,  2.209,  0.938). (\bar x, \bar y, \bar z) \approx (0.375,\; 2.209,\; 0.938). (xˉ,yˉ​,zˉ)≈(0.375,2.209,0.938).

Part 3 — The moment of inertia about the z-axis

Step 3.1: Set up the integral.

The squared distance to the zzz-axis is x2+y2x^2 + y^2x2+y2, which is exactly the factor of the density, so the integrand is (x2+y2)2(x^2 + y^2)^2(x2+y2)2:

Iz=∫0π/2 ⁣∫03 ⁣∫0rcos⁡θ/3(x2+y2)2 r dx dr dθ,with y2=r2cos⁡2θ. I_z = \int_0^{\pi/2}\!\int_0^3\!\int_0^{r\cos\theta/3} (x^2 + y^2)^2\, r\, dx\, dr\, d\theta, \qquad \text{with } y^2 = r^2\cos^2\theta. Iz​=∫0π/2​∫03​∫0rcosθ/3​(x2+y2)2rdxdrdθ,with y2=r2cos2θ.

Step 3.2: Evaluate with SymPy.

The script solution/part3_step3.py evaluates the integral in polar order and checks it against the Cartesian order 0≤z≤30 \le z \le 30≤z≤3, 0≤y≤9−z20 \le y \le \sqrt{9 - z^2}0≤y≤9−z2​, 0≤x≤y/30 \le x \le y/30≤x≤y/3; both agree exactly:

Iz=10464175≈59.7942857. I_z = \frac{10464}{175} \approx 59.7942857. Iz​=17510464​≈59.7942857.

Result (c). To three decimal places, Iz≈59.794. I_z \approx 59.794. Iz​≈59.794.

Step 3.3: Verification by Python.

All quantities were computed by the SymPy scripts solution/part1_step1.py, part2_step2.py, and part3_step3.py. The mass and moment of inertia were each evaluated in two independent orders of integration (polar in the yzyzyz-plane with xxx innermost, and pure Cartesian), and SymPy confirms the two forms agree exactly; the center of mass was verified to lie inside the solid. The figure script part1_figure1.py produces the figure embedded above.
